metadata.case_name: TSANG CHI CHEONG v. THE INCORPORATED OWNERS OF MEI KING MANSION (STAGE 1)

plaintiff.occupation_before: registered electrician (sole proprietor of Chiu Man Water, Electrical & Air-conditioning Engineering)

injuries.description: Superficial burn of the anterior part of the neck resulting in a slightly pigmented scar
source: he had sustained a "superficial burn" over the front part of his neck only.
The clinical diagnosis was neck burn injury.

As shown in the photo taken by the experts at the examination in April 2013, the scar is not obvious. The experts described it as a slightly pigmented scar over the anterior part of the neck measuring 110 mm x 90 mm.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of neck

manifestations.description: slightly pigmented scar over the anterior part of the neck measuring 110 mm x 90 mm
itchiness of the scar (worse in hot weather / when sweating)
neck pain (attended A&E again on 16 January 2009 for neck pain)

treatments_received: Attendance at Accident and Emergency Department, Queen Elizabeth Hospital (20:46 on date of Accident)
Follow-up at Kwun Tong General Out-patient Clinic on multiple occasions
treatments_future: Laser treatment (15 sessions) - recommended by Dr Chow (not accepted by court)

losses.description: Unsightly scar over the anterior neck (slightly pigmented) with intermittent itchiness, causing cosmetic concern
